description: A common and destructive bacterial disease affecting peppers, thriving in warm, humid weather. It causes leaf drop, fruit lesions, and reduced yield.
symptoms: Small, water-soaked circular to irregular dark brown spots with yellow halos on leaves. Lesions may enlarge, turn purplish-brown, and cause severe premature leaf dropping. Fruits develop rough, raised warty scabs.
severity_guidelines: Low: Isolated leaf spots on lower canopy (<15% foliage affected). Medium: Moderate spotting across mid-canopy with early leaf drop (15-35%). High: Severe defoliation, stem cankers, and fruit blistering (>35%).
diagnostic_cues: Water-soaked dark lesions with chlorotic yellow borders, rough warty blisters on fruit skin.

description: The pepper plant exhibits vigorous foliage, dark green coloration, absence of necrotic lesions, and normal vegetative or reproductive growth.
symptoms: Deep green, smooth, firm leaves without discoloration, spotting, wilting, or necrotic margins. Stems are sturdy and healthy.
severity_guidelines: None: Plant is in optimal health with 0% disease lesion coverage.
diagnostic_cues: Uniform chlorophyll distribution, intact leaf margins, lack of discoloration or lesions.

description: A fungal disease caused by Alternaria solani that primarily affects older foliage first, weakening the plant and impairing tuber bulking.
symptoms: Dark brown to black necrotic spots with characteristic concentric rings (target-like pattern), often surrounded by a chlorotic yellow halo. Starts on bottom leaves.
severity_guidelines: Low: Few target spots on bottom leaves (<15% foliage affected). Medium: Spreading to mid-canopy with yellowing foliage (15-35%). High: Extensive foliage blighting, premature vine death (>35%).
diagnostic_cues: Concentric bullseye rings inside dark angular spots bordered by leaf veins.

description: A devastating oomycete pathogen notorious for causing the Irish Potato Famine. Rapidly destroys potato foliage and rots tubers under cool, damp conditions.
symptoms: Water-soaked, dark green to purplish-black lesions that rapidly enlarge without sharp margins. Under high humidity, white downy mildew appears on leaf undersides.
severity_guidelines: Low: Sporadic dark water-soaked patches on leaf tips (<15%). Medium: Rapidly coalescing dark blotches with visible sporulation (15-35%). High: Complete canopy collapse, blackened rotting stems and tubers (>35%).
diagnostic_cues: Irregular water-soaked greasy lesions, white fungal mold on undersides during high humidity.

description: The potato plant shows robust foliage, rich green leaves, healthy stem vigor, and no indications of fungal, bacterial, or viral stress.
symptoms: Uniform vibrant green compound leaves, crisp turgid leaf stems, absence of blight spots or leaf curl.
severity_guidelines: None: Leaf surface is clean and undamaged with 0% disease lesion coverage.
diagnostic_cues: Vibrant green compound leaves with clear venation and zero spot lesions.

description: A widespread bacterial disorder leading to foliage blemishes and fruit spotting, significantly reducing marketable crop yield in warm, rainy climates.
symptoms: Small, dark circular spots that appear water-soaked initially, later turning dark brown to black with yellow halos. Leaf margins may become ragged.
severity_guidelines: Low: Scattered pinhead spots on lower leaves (<15%). Medium: Coalesced spots with yellowing surrounding tissue (15-35%). High: Heavy blighting, defoliation, and fruit scabbing (>35%).
diagnostic_cues: Small black speckles surrounded by bright yellow rings, translucent water-soaking on leaf back.

description: A ubiquitous fungal pathogen affecting tomatoes. It begins on lower, mature leaves and gradually progresses upward, causing defoliation and sunscald on exposed fruit.
symptoms: Dark brown to black circular lesions exhibiting distinctive concentric rings (target board pattern), surrounded by localized yellowing (chlorosis).
severity_guidelines: Low: A few lower leaves show target-board spots (<15%). Medium: Lesions spreading upward through the mid-canopy (15-35%). High: Widespread defoliation exposing green tomatoes to sunscald (>35%).
diagnostic_cues: Concentric rings resembling an archery target inside dark brown lesions, primarily on older leaves.

description: A fast-moving, destructive water mold that infects leaves, stems, and tomato fruits, capable of decimating an entire tomato patch within days of cool, wet weather.
symptoms: Large, irregular, greasy water-soaked gray-green spots rapidly turning dark brown or black. Stems develop dark brown lesions; white velvety sporulation on leaf undersides when humid.
severity_guidelines: Low: Isolated water-soaked blotches on outer leaf edges (<15%). Medium: Expanding dark blotches on multiple leaves and leaf stems (15-35%). High: Entire plant foliage wilts, blackens, and collapses with stem decay (>35%).
diagnostic_cues: Greasy, dark water-soaked patches with fuzzy white fungal growth on undersides in moist conditions.

description: The tomato plant exhibits lush, vibrant green compound foliage, balanced vegetative growth, clean stems, and zero signs of infectious lesions or deficiency symptoms.
symptoms: Bright or deep green leaflets with well-defined serrations, clean stems, active growth tips, and absence of chlorosis or necrosis.
severity_guidelines: None: Plant leaf is in pristine condition with 0% pathogen lesion presence.
diagnostic_cues: Uniform green pigmentation, unblemished leaf surface, normal leaflet morphology.
